title: Rooms he never saw · Seattle
logline: Chloe's Seattle apartment, empty, boxes by the door. A room the author never entered, drawn from a postcard and the divorce.

panels.composition: An apartment interior, imagined: tall windows, a city gray beyond, hardwood, a room emptied to its outlets. Three cardboard boxes by the door. On one, in her cramped capitals: BOOKS. On the windowsill, propped: a hand-drawn map of a city, folded and unfolded so many times it's soft — his 1999 map, in a room he never saw, the only object left. No people.

image.prompt: an emptied apartment with tall windows onto a gray city, bare hardwood, three cardboard boxes by the door, and on the windowsill a hand-drawn map folded soft with age, no people, spare ink with muted slate watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: The 1999 map (#33), kept, in a room he invents. Letter BOOKS after.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Drawn from nothing. The map on the sill is the sequence's argument.
